transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Well, I'm here because people keep acting like I'm just imagining it. But I know what I see. The hospital people... and some folks from the agency, they've been watching our house. They even watch my cleaning routes when I'm at work. They're doing it to see if I'm taking proper care of my husband.
If someone showed you clear proof that no one was watching your house or your routes, would you believe it?

No, I wouldn't. Because... well, I know what I'm seeing. 

People keep acting like I'm just making this up or imagining it, but I'm not. I see the hospital people, and I see the folks from the agency. They are watching our house. They watch my cleaning routes when I'm at work. They're doing it to check if I'm taking proper care of my husband. So, whatever proof someone thinks they have... it wouldn't change what I know is happening right in front of me.
Have you been feeling unusually depressed or down lately?

No, I haven't really been feeling down or depressed. I mean, it's stressful with them watching me all the time, making sure I'm doing things right for my husband, but... I wouldn't say I'm sad or anything like that. Just frustrated that no one believes me.
Have you had any periods when you felt unusually high, energetic, or ‘up’ compared with normal?

Yeah, I suppose there are times like that. There are stretches when I feel... just really bright and strong. Like I can handle absolutely everything without a problem. But during those times, if my husband or one of my cleaning clients questions me about something, I... well, I snap at them. Much harder than I actually mean to.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when the watching or other unusual beliefs were still there, but you were not feeling depressed or unusually energized at all?

Yes, actually. There was a stretch not too long ago... maybe for a few weeks or so. It was a quieter spell. I was sleeping more, just kind of a normal amount, and I wasn't rushing around feeling all that extra energy. I definitely wasn't depressed either. But... I still knew the agency was watching us. And I still heard that voice by the kitchen window. So the watching and the voice, they didn't go away, even when my mood was just steady.
Have you ever had a period lasting several days or longer when you felt so energetic or irritable that you needed much less sleep than usual?

Yes, definitely. There are times when I don't need much sleep at all. Many nights I'll only sleep for maybe two or three hours, and then I just... wake up. But I'm not tired like I used to be when I wouldn't get enough sleep. I wake up feeling completely ready to go, ready to scrub floors or sort through all my papers. It's like I don't even need the rest.
Have there been times when the voice or the belief that people were watching you continued even when you were not having a manic episode?

Yes, like I mentioned just a bit ago... there was that quieter spell. It lasted for several weeks, I think. I wasn't having all that extra energy, and I was sleeping a normal amount again. I wasn't rushing around cleaning or anything like that. But even then, I still heard the voice by the kitchen window. And I still knew the agency was watching us. So, yes, those things stayed even when I wasn't feeling so sped up.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt very depressed or lost interest or pleasure in most things?

No, I don't think so. I haven't really had a time where I felt down like that, or like I didn't want to do anything. I mean, I have those times where my mood is just steady, like I was saying, but I don't get depressed. It's usually just the extra energy or... just normal.
Have you ever had a period of at least one week when you felt so energized or irritable that it was a clear change from your usual self?

Yes, I have. There are stretches where I just feel... bright, you know? Like I'm really strong and can handle absolutely everything that comes my way. But during those same times, if my husband says something, or if one of my cleaning clients questions how I'm doing things, I just... I snap. I snap at them much harder than I mean to. It's definitely a change from how I usually am.
Have you ever had the voice or the belief that people were watching you only when you were feeling unusually energized or irritable, and not at other times?

Well, no, it's not *only* when I'm energized, like I said before. But they definitely happen at the same time, too. Like... during those weeks when I was hardly sleeping at all, and I was just running constantly from my cleaning jobs straight to church errands and back again. While all that was going on, I was still hearing that woman's voice. And I was absolutely certain that people were monitoring the routes I was taking. So, yes, it happens when I'm sped up, but not *only* then.
When you hear the voice, are you usually also feeling unusually energized or irritable at that same time?

Yeah, I would say so. For most of this whole change I've been going through, I've been really keyed up and irritable. I just feel driven to keep moving, you know? So even in the stretches when things aren't at their absolute worst, that energized feeling or that short temper is usually right there with it.
Have you ever had the voice or the belief that people were watching you at a time when you were not having any mood symptoms at all?

Yes, actually. There was a quieter spell for several weeks where I was sleeping more and just... not rushing around as much. My mood felt pretty normal. But even during that time, I still heard the voice by the kitchen window, and I still believed the agency was watching us. So, yes, it happens even when I'm not feeling all sped up or irritable.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when the voice or the belief that people were watching you continued while you were not having any manic or depressed symptoms at all?

Yeah, exactly like I was just saying. That quieter spell went on for several weeks. I wasn't feeling sped up or depressed at all—I was just sleeping a bit more and not rushing around as much with my cleaning jobs. But for those whole few weeks, I still heard that woman's voice by the kitchen window, and I still completely believed the agency was watching us. So, yes, it was definitely for more than two weeks.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when the voice or the belief that people were watching you continued while you were not having any manic or depressed symptoms at all?

I think you might have just asked me that, but yes. Like I just mentioned, it was definitely for more than two weeks. That quiet spell lasted a few weeks, and I wasn't having any of those mood issues, but I still heard the voice and felt like we were being watched the whole time.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you had the voice or the belief that people were watching you, but you did not have any manic symptoms at all?

Yes, doctor, I feel like we're going in circles a bit here, but yes. Like I've been saying, there was a quieter spell that lasted for several weeks. I was sleeping more and just... not rushing around as much to my cleaning jobs, so I didn't have any of those manic feelings. But even during those weeks, I still heard the voice by the kitchen window, and I still believed the agency was watching us.
Have you ever heard the voice or believed people were watching you for at least two weeks when you were not having any manic symptoms at all?

Doctor, I... I know I've answered this a few times now. Yes, it lasted for at least two weeks. Like I said, there was a quieter spell for several weeks where I wasn't having any of those manic symptoms. I was sleeping more, not rushing around to my cleaning jobs as much. But even during that whole time, I still heard the woman's voice by the kitchen window, and I still fully believed the agency was watching us.
Have you ever had the voice or the belief that people were watching you for at least two weeks when you were not having any manic or depressed symptoms at all?

I know we keep going over this, doctor, but yes. Like I've been saying, there was a quieter spell for several weeks. I wasn't having any of those mood problems at all—I was sleeping more and not rushing around as much to my cleaning jobs. But even during that whole quiet time, I still heard the voice by the kitchen window, and I still believed the agency was watching us.
During the quieter times when you were not feeling manic or depressed, did you still hear the voice or believe people were watching you?

Yes, I did. Like I mentioned before, there was that quieter stretch for a few weeks where my mood was just... normal, I guess. I wasn't overly energized or feeling down, just sleeping a bit more and taking my time with my cleaning jobs. But even then, without the mood stuff, I still heard that woman's voice by the window, and I still knew the agency had their eyes on us.
Have you ever had a period of at least one week when your mood was so elevated or irritable that it was a clear, distinct episode from your usual self?

Yes, I have. There are these stretches of time where I just feel... bright and strong. Like I can handle absolutely everything. But during those times, if my husband or one of my clients questions me about something, I... well, I snap at them much harder than I mean to. It's definitely a distinct change from how I normally am, and it can go on like that for a week or more.
Have there ever been times when the voice or belief that people were watching you happened only while you were having a manic episode?

Well, it didn't happen *only* during those times, because like I said, it happens when my mood is normal, too. But yes, it definitely happened while I was having those... elevated times. During the weeks when I was sleeping very little and running around from my cleaning jobs to church errands, I was also hearing that woman's voice by the window. And I was feeling absolutely certain that people were monitoring my routes while I was out working.

patient.answer: Well, it didn't happen *only* during those times, because like I said, it happens when my mood is normal, too. But yes, it definitely happened while I was having those... elevated times. During the weeks when I was sleeping very little and running around from my cleaning jobs to church errands, I was also hearing that woman's voice by the window. And I was feeling absolutely certain that people were monitoring my routes while I was out working.

opening_question.intent: Open the interview by eliciting the patient’s main concern and presenting complaint.
opening_question.question: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has clear psychotic symptoms (fixed persecutory delusion and auditory hallucination) occurring during a sustained mood episode with manic features, and crucially these psychotic symptoms also persisted for several weeks during a period without manic or depressive symptoms. This longitudinal pattern meets schizoaffective disorder criteria and argues against delusional disorder, which would not account for the recurrent auditory hallucination and mood episodes.
